ORDER Heard Sri S.M.Subhani, learned counsel representing Sri G.Suryam, learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Deputy Solicitor General appearing on behalf of the 1st respondent, Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of the 6th respondent, and Sri M.Anand Kumar, learned Standing Counsel SRS, J for National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) appearing on behalf of the respondents.
2. The writ petition is filed to declare the action of respondent No.5 in not considering the applications submitted by the petitioners dated 21.12.2023, as illegal and arbitrary.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the petitioners' land in Sy.No.14A/1B and 14B/2A an extent of Ac.0-13 cents, Ac.0-09 cents, Ac.0-09 cents and Ac.0-09 cents was acquired.
In Award No.4 of 2023 vide Rc.No.1525G1/NH//2017, dated 25.01.2023, the existence of Petrol Bunk is noted.
However, while determining compensation vide RC.B/1525/NH-340C/2022, dated 21.08.2023, no compensation was awarded in respect of the Petrol Bunk and structure.
The petitioners immediately filed applications dated 21.12.2023 under 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 before the learned Arbitrator.
The applications have been pending before the 5th respondent-The Arbitrator.
Learned counsel for the petitioners would further submit that pending the applications, the authorities are proceeding with the expansion work by demolishing the Petrol Bunk.
Hence, the writ petition.

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition did not dispute the pendency of applications made by the petitioners under Section 3(G)(5) of N.H.Act, 1956 r/w Sections 7 and 12 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (for short "the Act")before the 5th respondent.
5. Learned Standing Counsel for NHAI appearing on behalf of respondents 2 to 5 would submit that the learned Arbitrator will dispose of the applications as per Section 34 of the Act.

6. Thus, as seen from the material, there is no dispute about the acquisition of land, passing of the Award, and determination of compensation to the petitioners vide Proceedings RC.B.1525/NH- 340C/2022, dated 21.08.2023.
The grievance of the petitioners is that compensation was not awarded for the petrol bunk and structures and hence appropriate application was made.

7. Since the petitioners made applications under Section 3(G)(5) of the N.H.Act, before the 5th respondent, the 5th respondent- Arbitrator shall decide the matter as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of two (2) months, after receipt of copy of this order, by issuing notice and affording an opportunity of hearing to the petitioners, strictly in accordance with law.
SRS, J
If the respondent authorities are proceeding with the demolition of the Petrol Bunk, the petitioners shall make a necessary application before the Arbitrator.
The learned Arbitrator shall consider the same in accordance with law.
8. With the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of at the stage of admission with the consent of both the counsels.
No costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

JUSTICE SUBBA REDDY SATTI Date: 10.05.2024 KA SRS,
J THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE SUBBA REDDY SATTI WRIT PETITION No.11440 OF 2024 Date:
